title: AT THE HORNS OF THE ALTAR

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"The priest shall then put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of fragrant incense that is before the LORD in the tent of meeting. The rest of the bull's blood he shall pour out at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the entrance to the tent of meeting."'" - Lev 4:7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The altar of incense stood just before the curtain, and its fragrant smoke rose continually — a picture of prayer ascending to God. Blood is placed on its horns.

Think about what that means. Even the place of prayer needed cleansing.

That is a startling thought. We tend to assume that prayer is the one clean thing we do, our best offering, the part of us God surely approves. But Israel's worship acknowledged that even the altar of intercession was touched by human sin. Our prayers themselves need covering.

If you have ever finished praying and felt that your prayer was distracted, self-centred, or half-hearted — this verse is oddly comforting. Israel knew that too. And God provided for it.

Paul says the Spirit himself intercedes for us through wordless groans, because we do not know what we ought to pray for (Rom 8:26). And Christ, our High Priest, always lives to intercede for us (Heb 7:25). Your prayers do not reach the Father unaccompanied.

Then note the rest of the blood: poured out at the base of the altar, at the entrance. Most of it simply drained into the ground where everyone walked past. Grace is not stingy. There was more than enough.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I ever felt my prayers were too poor to be heard?
2. What difference does it make that Christ carries my prayers to the Father?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, even my prayers need Your mercy. Thank You that Christ intercedes for me and that my weak words reach You through Him. Amen.
